{"Address_address2":"Sector 54, SunCity, Golf Course Road","Email":"shikha@reach-to-teach.org","Address_address1":"Vatika Towers, Tower A,  4th Floor","Website1":"https://www.linkedin.com/company/reachtoteachin/about/","Website2":"","Number3":"230862","Formula":"49","Number2":"6170831","Number1":"5951486","MultiLine5":"In order to reach scale in a country the size of India, the only way to achieve this is through partnering with the Government. Reach to Teach partners with State Governments through a formal Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) as a knowledge and technical partner to support the Education Department in designing and rolling out large-scale academic reforms.Our idea of scaling is rooted in system strengthening, deep consultation, and working from within the existing Government education system to reach all Government schools in the State. We scale by embedding ourselves within the State Education Department which enables us to work across every level. Rather than setting up parallel structures, we co-create all interventions, curriculum design, training frameworks, implementation tools, and monitoring mechanisms, with system actors. By doing so, we create scalable solutions by using the Department and its functionaries as the force multipliers and do not need to staff-up. This approach ensures that with a small and agile team, we achieve State-wide coverage from inception by leverage existing Government outreach, infrastructure, and personnel, while building the system’s own capacity to deliver, adapt and sustain. This leads to rollout at scale, sustainability and a lasting improvement at a systems level. As the ownership of the process lies with the Government, and we ensure institutionalisation, our design has a clear exit strategy supported by documentation and a systematic handover process.","SingleLine2":"Reach To Teach Foundation","MultiLine7":"","SingleLine3":"Manoranjan Nayak","MultiLine1":"Every child will have access to quality education to enable them to become confident social citizens with improved life chances","SingleLine5":"Chief Operating Officer","MultiLine2":"We strive to improve education outcomes by making learning joyful, working with governments, partners, parents and communities, with foundational learning skills at the core.","MultiLine3":"The Reach to Teach Foundation works with State Governments on strengthening Leaning Outcomes in Government schools at scale by focusing on the twin elements of experiential learning and designing for teacher led interventions. We currently work in four States– Gujarat, Haryana, Arunachal Pradesh and Meghalaya – focusing on system realignment, scale and sustainability. Our work is based on design-led principles and we work with the Education Department and their functionaries and teachers to consult and design interventions collaboratively. This co-creation has led to ownership by the Department and we train district level functionaries and teachers through a ‘doing and learning’ approach on the use of the material and tools thus collaboratively designed. These people in turn become the State’s feet on street, implementing our design across every school in the State. It is a fully hands on model and has several advantages, The implementation is by the Government system across all Government schools in a State leading to system change at scale. This allows for a small team at our end to drive large-scale improvement. We have Project Management Units embedded in the State Council for Educational Research and Training (SCERT) and a dedicated helpline for continuous support to teachers and other functionaries in the value chain. We have set up communities of practice by creating subject-wise, District- wise WhatsApp groups which are both sounding boards but also a place for teachers and other functionaries to share anxieties, success and good practice.  Within 2 to 3 years of working in Arunachal Pradesh, the Board Exam results have improved significantly and the National Assessment Survey, a national Indice measuring competency based learning amongst students has seen the State climb up from being 35 out of 36 States and UTs to being in the 17th position this year.","Address_zipCode":"122003","MultiLine4":"Across the states where we operate, our programs are creating measurable impact, with outcomes consistently reflected in national-level indices, demonstrating the effectiveness and reach of our work.

Arunachal Pradesh: 
1)PARAKH (erstwhile National Achievement Survey,NAS) 2023–24: Arunachal Pradesh has shown a marked improvement in NAS 2023-24. Outperformed the national average in Language subjects for both Class 6 and Class 9. And In Grade 3 Arunachal Pradesh has surpassed its 2017 performance levels. Language gap with national average reduced from 11 points (2021) to 5 points (2024). Math gap reduced from 13 points (2021) to 6 points (2024).
2)CBSE Board Examination Results (2023–25): Significant improvement in Board Exam results over two years—2023–24 and 2024–25. Achieved a cumulative increase of 15.58% in the Class 10 pass percentage and a 16.17% increase in the Class 12 pass percentage compared to 2022–23—far surpassing the benchmarks established by the State Cabinet.
3)SDG India Index 2024: Arunachal Pradesh improved 11 points in SDG-4 Quality Education in SDG India Index Report 2024, Highest in the North-East Sates and transitioned from an ASPIRANT to a PERFORMER state.
4)Performance Grading Index (PGI) 2023–24: Arunachal Pradesh has advanced in the latest PGI rankings, 21.8 points improvement over the previous year's score with notable enhancements in Governance Processes, Teacher Education, and Infrastructure domains.

Meghalaya: 
1)PARAKH (erstwhile National Achievement Survey,NAS) 2023–24: Meghalaya has shown measurable progress in foundational and overall learning outcomes between 2021 and 2024. The state recorded notable gains in early-grade Mathematics (+8 points) and Language (+6 points), significantly narrowing the learning gap with national averages.
2)PGI 2023-24: Meghalaya has demonstrated improvement of 16.3 points in the latest PGI rankings compared to the previous year. This progress is primarily attributed to advancements in Access, Infrastructure, Governance Processes, and Teacher Education.

Gujarat: 
1)Reduced “hard spots” in Grades 3–8 from 180 to 133—a 25% improvement in addressing core learning gaps.
2)PGI 2023-24: Gujarat has scored 614 (out of 1000) ranked 3rd in the PGI 2023-24, Moved from 5th Rank in 2021 to 3rd Rank in the country with the improvement of 22 points

Haryana
1)School Accreditation: A comprehensive School Quality Assessment and Accreditation Framework (SQAAF) for Haryana was developed by Reach to Teach. Framework was launched by Manohar Lal Khattar, Chief Minister, Haryana and Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan in PM Schools for Rising India(PMSHRI) event held in Rohtak on 24th October 2023. The programme has been scaled to 1789 (round 1) schools in Haryana.

{"Name_First":"Faith","Name_Last":"Ndung'u","SingleLine":"Executive Director","SingleLine2":"Go Economic Empowerment  Progrmme GEEP KENYA","Email":"geepkenya@gmail.com","Website":"https://geepkenya.org/","Website1":"http://www.linkedin.com/in/geep-kenya-a92404116","Website2":"","Dropdown":"Yes","Name5_First":"Faith","Name5_Last":"Ndung'u","Email1":"geepkenya@gmail.com","Dropdown1":"Yes","Name4_First":"Faith","Name4_Last":"Ndung'u","SingleLine5":"Executive Director","Email2":"geepkenya@gmail.com","MonthYear":"Jun-2014","Dropdown2":"Non-profit","Dropdown3":"Kenya","MultipleChoice":["Kenya"],"Dropdown4":"Yes, all of the countries","MultiLine":"","MultiLine1":"To be a leading force in economic empowerment across Africa, transforming communities through sustainable livelihoods and breaking the cycle of poverty for future generations.","MultiLine2":"To partner with communities in creating sustainable livelihoods, ending hunger, reducing poverty, and protecting the rights of children and vulnerable households.","MultiLine3":"1. Child Protection & Care Reform Program
This program strengthens family-based care and community child protection systems in line with the Children Act (2022) and the National Care Reform Strategy (2022–2032).
Key components:
•	Reintegration of children from Charitable Children’s Institutions (CCIs)
•	Family strengthening and case management
•	Training Community Volunteer Children Officers (CVCOs) and community structures
•	Safeguarding training for caregivers, parents, and youth
•	Inclusion of children with disabilities through linkages, therapy support, and assistive devices

2. Early Childhood Development (ECD) & Home-Based Childcare (HBCC) Support Program
Focused on improving early learning and nutrition outcomes for children aged 0–3 in informal and formal childcare settings.
Key components:
•	Training HBCC providers on ECD, stimulation, and responsive caregiving
•	Nutrition improvement through kitchen gardens and practical feeding demonstrations
•	Supporting parents with ECD knowledge and parenting skills
•	Enhancing safety, learning materials, and environments in informal daycares

3. Agroecology, Food Security & Nutrition ProgramThis program empowers households, HBCC providers, and schools to produce nutritious food sustainably through climate-smart and agroecological practices.
Key components:
•	Vertical and portable kitchen gardens for households and HBCC centres
•	School Gardens to promote nutrition education, agroecology learning, and greening of school environments
•	Indigenous vegetables, diversified diets, and seed preservation
•	Organic farming and soil health restoration
•	Rainwater harvesting and water-use efficiency
•	Nutrition education for parents, caregivers, teachers, and youth groups
School Gardens are implemented as part of this program and provide practical learning opportunities, improve child nutrition, and strengthen sustainable food systems in schools.

4. Economic Empowerment & Livelihoods Program
Designed to improve family income, resilience, and financial inclusion.
Key components:
•	Group Savings and Loan Associations 
•	Entrepreneurship and financial literacy training
•	Small business grants and mentorship
•	Dairy goats support for vulnerable families and HBCC providers
•	Youth livelihoods and skills development
•	Social protection linkages (e.g., NHIF, Inua Jamii, government programs)

5. Education, Life Skills & Youth Empowerment Program
Promotes learning outcomes, youth engagement, and holistic development.
Key components:
•	Literacy and numeracy programs in partnership with Usawa Agenda and Zizi Afrique
•	Life Skills and Values (ALiVE initiative)
•	School mentorship and girl empowerment sessions
•	Support for vulnerable learners to remain in school
•	Youth leadership, advocacy, and participation in community change

6. Health, Advocacy & Awareness Program
Works to improve the health and well-being of women, youth, and vulnerable community members.
Key components:
•	HIV/AIDS awareness, stigma reduction, and linkage to care
•	Mental health awareness, psychosocial support, and referrals
•	Menstrual health education and pad distribution
•	GBV/SGBV prevention, reporting pathways, and survivor support
•	Adolescents’ sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) dialogues

7. Environmental Conservation & Climate Action Program
Strengthens climate resilience and promotes environmental stewardship.
Key components:
•	Tree planting and school greening initiatives
•	Youth-led climate action and conservation campaigns
•	Clean-up drives, waste management, and environmental hygiene
•	Climate education integrated into school and community settings

8. Research, Advocacy & Policy Engagement Program
Evidence generation and advocacy efforts that influence policy and practice across all sectors.
Key components:
•	Policy research, learning documentation, and dissemination

{"Name_First":"Faith","Name_Last":"Ndung'u","SingleLine":"Executive Director","SingleLine2":"Go Economic Empowerment  Progrmme GEEP KENYA","Email":"geepkenya@gmail.com","Website":"https://geepkenya.org/","Website1":"http://www.linkedin.com/in/geep-kenya-a92404116","Website2":"","Dropdown":"Yes","Name5_First":"Faith","Name5_Last":"Ndung'u","Email1":"geepkenya@gmail.com","Dropdown1":"Yes","Name4_First":"Faith","Name4_Last":"Ndung'u","SingleLine5":"Executive Director","Email2":"geepkenya@gmail.com","MonthYear":"Jun-2014","Dropdown2":"Non-profit","Dropdown3":"Kenya","MultipleChoice":["Kenya"],"Dropdown4":"Yes, all of the countries","MultiLine":"","MultiLine1":"To be a leading force in economic empowerment across Africa, transforming communities through sustainable livelihoods and breaking the cycle of poverty for future generations.","MultiLine2":"To partner with communities in creating sustainable livelihoods, ending hunger, reducing poverty, and protecting the rights of children and vulnerable households.","MultiLine3":"1. Child Protection & Care Reform Program
This program strengthens family-based care and community child protection systems in line with the Children Act (2022) and the National Care Reform Strategy (2022–2032).
Key components:
•	Reintegration of children from Charitable Children’s Institutions (CCIs)
•	Family strengthening and case management
•	Training Community Volunteer Children Officers (CVCOs) and community structures
•	Safeguarding training for caregivers, parents, and youth
•	Inclusion of children with disabilities through linkages, therapy support, and assistive devices

2. Early Childhood Development (ECD) & Home-Based Childcare (HBCC) Support Program
Focused on improving early learning and nutrition outcomes for children aged 0–3 in informal and formal childcare settings.
Key components:
•	Training HBCC providers on ECD, stimulation, and responsive caregiving
•	Nutrition improvement through kitchen gardens and practical feeding demonstrations
•	Supporting parents with ECD knowledge and parenting skills
•	Enhancing safety, learning materials, and environments in informal daycares

3. Agroecology, Food Security & Nutrition ProgramThis program empowers households, HBCC providers, and schools to produce nutritious food sustainably through climate-smart and agroecological practices.
Key components:
•	Vertical and portable kitchen gardens for households and HBCC centres
•	School Gardens to promote nutrition education, agroecology learning, and greening of school environments
•	Indigenous vegetables, diversified diets, and seed preservation
•	Organic farming and soil health restoration
•	Rainwater harvesting and water-use efficiency
•	Nutrition education for parents, caregivers, teachers, and youth groups
School Gardens are implemented as part of this program and provide practical learning opportunities, improve child nutrition, and strengthen sustainable food systems in schools.

4. Economic Empowerment & Livelihoods Program
Designed to improve family income, resilience, and financial inclusion.
Key components:
•	Group Savings and Loan Associations 
•	Entrepreneurship and financial literacy training
•	Small business grants and mentorship
•	Dairy goats support for vulnerable families and HBCC providers
•	Youth livelihoods and skills development
•	Social protection linkages (e.g., NHIF, Inua Jamii, government programs)

5. Education, Life Skills & Youth Empowerment Program
Promotes learning outcomes, youth engagement, and holistic development.
Key components:
•	Literacy and numeracy programs in partnership with Usawa Agenda and Zizi Afrique
•	Life Skills and Values (ALiVE initiative)
•	School mentorship and girl empowerment sessions
•	Support for vulnerable learners to remain in school
•	Youth leadership, advocacy, and participation in community change

6. Health, Advocacy & Awareness Program
Works to improve the health and well-being of women, youth, and vulnerable community members.
Key components:
•	HIV/AIDS awareness, stigma reduction, and linkage to care
•	Mental health awareness, psychosocial support, and referrals
•	Menstrual health education and pad distribution
•	GBV/SGBV prevention, reporting pathways, and survivor support
•	Adolescents’ sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) dialogues

7. Environmental Conservation & Climate Action Program
Strengthens climate resilience and promotes environmental stewardship.
Key components:
•	Tree planting and school greening initiatives
•	Youth-led climate action and conservation campaigns
•	Clean-up drives, waste management, and environmental hygiene
•	Climate education integrated into school and community settings

8. Research, Advocacy & Policy Engagement Program
Evidence generation and advocacy efforts that influence policy and practice across all sectors.

•	Policy research, learning documentation, and dissemination
•	Community, school, and stakeholder dialogues
•	Evidence-based advocacy in child protection, education, climate, and livelihoods

These partnerships enhance coordination, strengthen service delivery, and support the alignment of programmes with existing government systems and policies—an approach that offers valuable learning for other non-state education actors seeking to work within and alongside public systems.

Through initiatives that support diversified livelihoods, small business growth, and financial inclusion, the organisation enhances the capacity of households to sustainably support children’s education and well-being. This integrated economic empowerment model provides practical insights for education actors on addressing the socio-economic barriers that affect access to, retention in, and completion of education.
The organisation also demonstrates strong advocacy capacity, particularly in promoting child protection, care reform, and inclusion. Its advocacy efforts are grounded in evidence generated through research and informed by community engagement, enabling it to influence policy and practice effectively. By working to strengthen systems that support children in need of care and protection, the organisation ensures that children’s rights, safety, and well-being are prioritized across interventions. This rights-based, systems-strengthening approach offers transferable lessons for other non-state education actors seeking to embed child protection and inclusion within their programmes.","MultiLine2":"While the organisation has a strong and integrated education model that combines inclusive formal education, vocational training, and life skills development, participation in a community of education organisations could further strengthen several aspects of its work.

Being part of an education network would enable the organisation to benchmark its VET models, adopt innovative approaches, and enhance pathways from skills training to employment or entrepreneurship.

This would enhance the measurement of outcomes related to learner resilience, employability, and socio-economic mobility.
Finally, engagement in a broader education community would strengthen the organisation’s ability to contribute to and learn from collective advocacy, research, and systems-strengthening efforts. {"Address_address2":"Pocket 9, Sector B, Vasant Kunj, New Delhi, Delhi 110070","Email":"ankit@idreamcareer.com","Address_address1":"2nd Floor, Boulder Box Building,","Website1":"https://www.linkedin.com/company/idreamcareer-com/","Website2":"","Number3":"498","Formula":"50","Number2":"20000000","Number1":"200000","MultiLine5":"iDreamCareer engages closely with government bodies through both financial and non-financial partnerships to support the institutionalization of career guidance within public education systems. Under financial agreements, iDreamCareer has directly implemented paid career guidance programs funded by government institutions, including RMSA Andhra Pradesh in 2018, CBSE in 2025, and the District Education Office, Sundargarh in Odisha in 2024, covering program design, deployment, and outcome monitoring. 

Alongside this, iDreamCareer has worked through several non-financial and grant-supported government partnerships focused on system design, capacity building, and piloting scalable models. This includes collaboration with EVGC Delhi, initially supported by Central Square Foundation, followed by UNDP and Tata Power DDL, to embed career guidance within Delhi government schools. iDreamCareer has also partnered with the Department of Secondary Education, Uttar Pradesh under a non-financial agreement with program funding provided by Mahindra Social Responsibility Foundation. In addition, iDreamCareer has engaged with New Delhi Municipal Council and Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation to support career guidance initiatives within municipal school systems; NDMC and BMC are among the richest municipal corporations in India, and these partnerships demonstrate iDreamCareer’s ability to work with financially strong urban local bodies as well as state education systems, combining public funding, external philanthropy, and technical expertise to enable scalable and sustainable adoption of career guidance.","SingleLine2":"iDreamCareer","MultiLine7":"iDreamCareer is a mission-driven social enterprise operating through a dual-entity structure that allows us to combine scale, sustainability, and impact. Our work is delivered through a for-profit entity, Medhavi Professional Services Pvt Ltd (branded as iDreamCareer), and a Section 8 not-for-profit organization, Aasman Foundation, which holds valid FCRA registration. This structure enables us to work seamlessly with governments, schools, CSR programs, and philanthropic funders, while ensuring financial sustainability and long-term system adoption.

Our social impact work is anchored under PathShila, which focuses on enabling equitable access to career guidance for students from government and underserved school systems, while advocating for the institutionalization of career counseling within public education. Across all our work, we leverage technology as a core enabler—using digital platforms and AI to support students in receiving personalized guidance, empower counselors to deliver structured and efficient interventions, and help systems measure outcomes such as enrolment, persistence, and transitions. By combining on-ground delivery, capacity building, and technology, iDreamCareer works to move career guidance from fragmented interventions to a measurable, system-level solution that supports successful education-to-employment transitions at scale.","SingleLine3":"Manish Chourasia","MultiLine1":"To enable every learner—regardless of background—to make informed, confident, and aspirational education-to-employment decisions, and to unlock equitable economic mobility at scale.","SingleLine5":"Director PathShila","MultiLine2":"By 2030, iDreamCareer aims to enable informed, equitable, and aspirational education-to-employment transitions for over 11 million learners—reaching 1 million students through direct classroom and counseling programs and 10 million learners through system-level adoption with governments and institutions.","MultiLine3":"iDreamCareer’s core program is a system-led, technology-enabled career guidance model designed to support learners across school and post-school transitions while strengthening the institutions that serve them. The program combines direct student engagement, counselor capacity development, and digital platforms to ensure high-quality guidance at scale, and is delivered through paid partnerships with governments, schools, and institutions, making it sustainable and scalable.

At the center of the program is PathShila, iDreamCareer’s impact practice, which works primarily with students from government and low-income schools. PathShila delivers structured career guidance directly to students while advocating for the adoption of career counseling within government education systems. Through partnerships with state and district governments, NGOs, CSR programs, and philanthropic organizations, PathShila focuses on creating tangible, measurable impact and enabling career guidance to transition from short-term projects to a system-embedded public service.

Complementing this is BlueSpring, the private school practice, which works with private and international schools to integrate career guidance into the school ecosystem. BlueSpring delivers grade-wise, structured career guidance programs that support students and parents in making informed academic and career decisions, while helping schools institutionalize career guidance as a core offering.

To ensure long-term quality and scale, iDreamCareer runs Council, a capacity development initiative focused on strengthening the career counseling ecosystem. Council works with counselors across government systems, private schools, NGOs, and independent practice, providing training, certification, standardized frameworks, and continuous professional development to professionalize and scale high-quality career counseling.

All programs are enabled by iDC One, iDreamCareer’s AI-enabled career guidance platform, which supports students in receiving personalized guidance, enables counselors to deliver structured and efficient interventions, and allows schools and governments to monitor delivery quality, scale, and student transition outcomes over time. Together, these elements form a unified core program that moves career guidance from isolated interventions to a sustainable, system-level solution focused on informed education-to-employment transitions.","Address_zipCode":"110070","MultiLine4":"iDreamCareer’s impact is demonstrated through measurable improvements in Eligible Enrolment Ratio (EER) and stronger education-to-employment transitions driven by structured career guidance and system adoption. An independent impact evaluation conducted in December 2025 across five districts of Uttar Pradesh—Ghaziabad, Kanpur, Lucknow, Meerut, and Varanasi—found that students in schools supported by iDreamCareer consistently recorded higher enrolment levels than comparison schools at both baseline and endline, with these differences being statistically significant (Pearson chi-square value of 29.96). While year-on-year changes in enrolment remained relatively stable across both treatment and comparison groups, resulting in a near-zero Difference-in-Differences estimate, the findings highlight that treatment schools maintained structurally stronger EER outcomes over time. This demonstrates that career guidance delivers its greatest value when embedded within education systems rather than implemented as short-term projects. By enabling governments and institutions to adopt standardized career guidance frameworks, trained counselors, and technology platforms, iDreamCareer has strengthened system capacity to support informed enrolment decisions at scale, improve the quality of transitions, and sustain education-to-employment outcomes for large student populations","Number11":"55","Number10":"50","Name_Last":"Bansal","MultipleChoice":["India"],"SingleLine31":"","SingleLine32":"","Dropdown":"No","SubForm1":[{"firstName":"Ayush","lastName":"Bansal","email7":"ayush@idreamcareer.com"},{"firstName":"Praveen","lastName":"Kumar","email7":"praveen@idreamcareer.com"}],"MultipleChoice2":["Education technology","System strengthening","Teacher development and certification"],"MultipleChoice1":["Grade 8","Grade 9","Grade 10","Grade 11","Grade 12"],"MultipleChoice4":null,"MultipleChoice3":["AI and education","Secondary education and work readiness"],"Dropdown9":"Yes","Name5_First":"Ayush","Name5_Last":"Bansal","Dropdown4":"Yes, all of the countries","Dropdown3":"India","Dropdown2":"For-profit","Dropdown1":"Yes","Dropdown8":"Low income ($2.01 - $10 a day)","Dropdown6":"Other","SingleLine":"Director PathShila","Dropdown5":"Yes","Dropdown10":"Yes","Dropdown11":null,"Dropdown12":"Students","Dropdown13":null,"Radio2":"Yes","Radio1":"Yes","Dropdown15":"GSF LinkedIn","MonthYear":"Dec-2013","Website":"https://idreamcareer.com/","Name_First":"Ankit","MultiLine":"","Name4_First":"Ankit","Name4_Last":"Bansal","Number":"2000","Email6":"manish.chourasia@idreamcareer.com","SubForm":[{"firstName":"Samar","lastName":"Bajaj","jobTitle":"Head of Education, India","organisation":"MSDF","email":"samar.bajaj@dell.org"},{"firstName":"Mukesh","lastName":"Sharma","jobTitle":"Menterra Venture Advisors","organisation":"Co-founder and Head of Investments at Menterra","email":"mukesh@menterra.com"}],"Email1":"ayush@idreamcareer.com","Email2":"ankit@idreamcareer.com","Address_country":"India","Address_city":"New Delhi,"}

Since its founding, over 1500 children have had access to a quality education. It also supports students who continue their secondary and post-secondary education.

Registered as an indigenous NGO, Hope for Youth Uganda is dedicated to breaking the cycle of poverty and giving marginalized children the tools they need to create brighter futures. Hope for Youth Uganda's mission is to provide opportunities for children and young adults to cultivate and utilize their talents and skills for the purpose of improving their economic emancipation from poverty levels through education and community projects. It ensures that every child, no matter their background, has access to the quality education, skills, and opportunities they need to thrive.

H4YU provides a safe space where young people can grow, learn, and develop life skills. It embodies an experiential learning philosophy in action to encourage holistic development. Programs are strength-based through expressive arts and organized co-curricular activities.

The All-Stars program empowers youth through creativity, expression, and active engagement. Using sports, music, dance, and drama, the program provides both educational and emotional support while offering young people a platform to share stories, showcase talents, and build confidence. Beyond personal growth, All-Stars serves as a community mobilization tool, identifying local volunteers and delivering health education and prevention initiatives through music and dance. Competitions between schools and villages further engage youth, helping them develop skills, knowledge, and resilience to stay safe and thrive.

Development School for Youth (DSY) equips young people with the leadership, communication, and professional skills they need to become future changemakers. Designed for aspiring leaders, the program combines training, mentorship, and real-world experience to prepare participants for success in their communities and careers. In partnership with corporate professionals and organizations, DSY provides hands-on learning opportunities and internship placements that bridge the gap between education and employment, empowering our graduates to lead with purpose and impact.

The You Matter Girls Club offers a safe and empowering space for teen schoolgirls and young mothers to freely express themselves, share experiences, and engage in meaningful discussions. The Grandmothers and Nutrition program celebrates the vital role grandmothers play in nurturing our community’s children and youth. By valuing their contributions and fostering meaningful connections with young people, the program creates a cycle of learning, care, and respect across generations.

When expanded at school level, the approach showed broader improvements in attendance and performance, providing early evidence that psychosocial support can positively influence educational outcomes.","SingleLine8":"In 2025, the organization signed MoUs with the schoolsit will be working with in preparation for the work to start in 2026.","SingleLine34":"As a newly registered organisation, it remains at an early stage of institutional maturity, with most activities still in the pilot and system-design phase and limited evidence of long-term impact at scale. Current reliance on a small volunteer team may constrain operational capacity, monitoring, and growth. Scaling the model sustainably will require strengthened organisational systems, stable funding, and deeper partnerships with schools and authorities. The organisation’s success is also dependent on sustained buy-in from external stakeholders, and as it grows, there will be an increasing need to formalise governance, financial management, and monitoring and evaluation frameworks to support expansion and risk management.","SingleLine33":"The organisation demonstrates a strong and clearly articulated understanding of the psychosocial challenges affecting learners in underserved communities and positions emotional wellbeing as a critical driver of attendance, retention, and academic performance. Its approach is grounded in direct classroom experience and supported by baseline data, lending credibility to both problem identification and programme design. The programmatic model is coherent and holistic, combining safe spaces for learners, capacity building for teachers, and peer support mechanisms. In addition, the organisation shows strong safeguarding readiness, with comprehensive policies and high responsiveness during due diligence, and benefits from being youth-led with leadership that is closely aligned to the mission and context.","SingleLine35":"Joining GSF would support the organisation’s growth by providing access to a global peer network, shared learning, and practical insights from more established education organisations, helping to strengthen programme quality, safeguarding, governance, and monitoring systems. Membership would also enhance the organisation’s credibility and visibility, enabling stronger partnerships with funders, schools, and policymakers, while reducing early-stage risks and supporting responsible, sustainable scaling of its psychosocial support model within the education ecosystem.","SingleLine36":"The organisation would contribute to GSF by bringing strong grassroots insights and practitioner-led experience on integrating psychosocial and emotional wellbeing into school systems in low-resource contexts. Its data-informed, youth-led approach would add valuable perspectives to peer learning on learner wellbeing, safe spaces, and teacher capacity building, particularly in regions affected by poverty, instability, and high dropout rates. Through active participation in GSF’s community, the organisation would share lessons from piloting and embedding psychosocial support within existing school structures, contributing to collective learning, innovation, and the strengthening of holistic education approaches across the network.","SingleLine12":"the organisation is currently early-stage and primarily volunteer-led, with no formal long-term funding streams articulated at this stage. Its activities to date appear to have been supported through in-kind contributions, volunteer time, and modest, locally driven resources while systems, governance, and pilot programmes are being developed. The organisation is still in the foundational phase, focusing on designing sustainable models within existing school and community structures, and is expected to seek partnerships and external funding as it moves from piloting toward scale."}

At that time, we were colleagues working in education, but over the years our relationship has grown into one where I have supported and guided him as he developed Psych Care Uganda.
I have been present from the early days, when Psych Care Uganda was still an idea shaped by Vicent’s firsthand experience working with young children especially adolescents  in schools and seeing how unmet mental health needs were affecting learning and wellbeing. Since then, I have continued to offer mentorship, advice, and practical support as the organisation has grown into a structured, community-based organisation delivering school and community mental health programs in Mayuge district in eastern Uganda.
This close relationship has allowed me to clearly see both Vicent’s leadership and the organisation’s commitment to doing meaningful, grounded work with adolescents.","signerEmail":"ykasakya9@gmail.com","signatureFieldName":"email","subformEntryIndex":"1","applicationUid":"4ebcb8ec-e92c-4c04-b74b-ae53589d2286","MultiLine1":"One of Psych Care Uganda’s strongest qualities is how closely its work is connected to the real experiences of learners, teachers, and schools. The organisation was not created from theory, but from lived experience in classrooms and communities where mental health support is missing.
Psych Care Uganda has shown that it is possible to integrate mental health into schools in a way that feels practical and respectful of local realities. Their use of peer led clubs, safe spaces for adolescents, and teacher support approaches are simple, thoughtful, and easy for schools to engage with.
Another clear strength is Vicent’s leadership. He leads with empathy, listens carefully to feedback, and is deeply committed to young people. This has helped the organisation build trust with local leaders, schools and communities, which is often one of the hardest parts of this kind of work.
These experiences and approaches are valuable lessons that could be shared with other non state education actors.","MultiLine2":"Psych Care Uganda is currently operating without formal funding and relies heavily on personal commitment, volunteer support, and strong relationships with local leaders at the district, schools and community members. Being part of this community (Global Schools Forum) would significantly strengthen Psych Care Uganda’s work. Access to peer organisations would support learning on how to responsibly scale school based mental health programs, strengthen its internal systems, and build a long-term sustainability. it would also expose Psych Care Uganda to funding networks, partners, and shared fundraising strategies which are crucial at this stage. This will allow the organisation to move from resource constrained delivery to more stable and scalable implementation.
At the same time, Psych Care Uganda would bring practical experience and grounded perspectives to the community, particularly around delivering mental health support in underserved school settings where the need is high but funding is often limited.","MultiLine3":"From my experience, Psych Care Uganda is genuinely collaborative in how it works with others. Box 972","Website1":"","Website2":"https://x.com/aid_for16765/header_photo","Number3":"83","Number2":"4300","Number1":"3200","MultiLine5":"","SingleLine2":"Asante Aid for Children and Schools in Africa","MultiLine7":"Asante Aid Organisation is more than an education NGO; we are a community-driven movement for dignity, equity, and opportunity. What sets us apart is our unwavering commitment to transparency, accountability, and collaboration. Every initiative we undertake is backed by clear budgets, open reporting, and active community participation, ensuring that donors and partners can trust both our vision and our execution.

We are proud to combine local leadership with global partnerships. Our founder and team work directly with communities in Kilifi, Mombasa, Kwale, Tana River, Taita Taveta, and beyond, while also engaging with international networks to share best practices and scale their impact. This dual approach allows us to remain deeply rooted in local realities while contributing to global conversations on education equity.

Our organisation also invests heavily in digital advocacy and storytelling, using blogs, social media, and multimedia campaigns to amplify the voices of children, parents, and teachers. This not only mobilizes resources but also builds a culture of empathy and shared responsibility across borders.

Above all, we see education as a transformative force for generations. By integrating housing, healthcare, mobility, and climate-smart solutions into our education programs, we ensure that learning is holistic, sustainable, and future-ready.","SingleLine3":"Dr Habil Slade Ogalo","MultiLine1":"At Asante Aid Organisation, we envision an Africa where every child, regardless of background or circumstance, has access to quality, inclusive, and transformative education. We believe education is not only a pathway out of poverty but also the foundation for building resilient, innovative, and compassionate communities.","SingleLine5":"CEO/Founder","MultiLine2":"Asante Aid Organisation exists to empower children and communities across Africa through equitable, inclusive, and transformative education. We are committed to breaking down barriers of poverty, disability, and marginalization by ensuring that every child has the opportunity to learn, thrive, and make meaningful contributions to society.","MultiLine3":"1. Inclusive Education Access  
We build and support schools in rural and marginalized communities, ensuring safe, inclusive, and child-friendly learning environments. Our focus is on children who are often excluded due to poverty, disability, or geography.

2. Teacher Training & Professional Development  
We provide continuous training, mentorship, and resources for teachers to strengthen pedagogy, leadership, and classroom management. This program equips educators with modern tools to deliver quality, learner-centered education.

3. Holistic Child Support  
Recognizing that education thrives when children’s basic needs are met, we integrate health, nutrition, housing, and mobility support into our programs. This includes initiatives like medical aid, wheelchair provision, and housing support for vulnerable families.

4. Climate-Smart & Sustainable Schools  
We embed sustainability into education by implementing solar-powered water pumps, green classrooms, and climate education. This ensures schools are resilient, environmentally conscious, and future-ready.

5. Digital Advocacy & Community Engagement  
Through blogs, social media, and storytelling, we amplify community voices, mobilize resources, and inspire global action. This program strengthens transparency, donor trust, and community ownership of education initiatives.

6. Strategic Partnerships & Collaboration  
We actively collaborate with local leaders, governments, and global networks like GSF to co-create solutions, share expertise, and scale impact across Africa.","Address_zipCode":"801O8","MultiLine4":"Through our programs, Asante Aid Organisation has transformed access to education for vulnerable children in rural Kenya. We have:

Reached underserved communities by building inclusive learning spaces and supporting children who would otherwise be excluded due to poverty, disability, or geography.

Improved teaching quality by training and mentoring educators, resulting in stronger literacy, numeracy, and life skills outcomes.

Enhanced child well-being by integrating health, nutrition, housing, and mobility support, ensuring children are healthy and ready to learn.

Promoted sustainability through climate-smart initiatives like solar-powered water pumps and green classrooms, making schools resilient and future-ready.

Amplified community voices via digital advocacy, mobilizing resources and building donor trust through transparent communication.

The result: children who were once at risk of dropping out are now thriving in school, teachers are better equipped to deliver quality education, and communities are empowered to sustain progress.","Number10":"40","Name_Last":"Ondiek","MultipleChoice":["Kenya"],"SingleLine31":"","SingleLine32":"","Dropdown":"Yes","SubForm1":[{"firstName":"Henry","lastName":"Gatty","email7":"henry.gatty@gmail.com"},{"firstName":"Nicholas","lastName":"Ondiek","email7":"info@asanteaid.org"}],"MultipleChoice1":["ECED (0-3 years)","ECED (3-6 years)","Grade 1","Grade 2","Grade 3","Grade 4","Grade 5","Grade 6","Grade 7","Grade 8","Grade 9","Grade 10","Grade 11","Grade 12"],"MultipleChoice4":null,"MultipleChoice3":["Childcare and ECED","Girls education","Inclusive education","Secondary education and work readiness"],"Dropdown9":"No","Name5_First":"Nicholas","Name5_Last":"Ondiek","Dropdown4":"Yes, all of the countries","Dropdown3":"Kenya","Dropdown2":"Non-profit","Dropdown1":"Yes","Dropdown8":"Poor (less than $2 a day)","Dropdown6":"Free","SingleLine":"CEO/Founder","Dropdown5":"Zero fees","Dropdown10":"Yes","Dropdown11":"No","Dropdown13":"Yes, all our schools","Radio2":"Yes","Radio1":"Yes","Dropdown15":"Search engine","MonthYear":"Oct-2012","Website":"www.asanteaid.org","Name_First":"Nicholas","MultiLine":"","Name4_First":"Nicholas","Name4_Last":"Ondiek","Number":"8","Email6":"drhabilslade@gmail.com","SubForm":[{"firstName":"Jennee","lastName":"Galland","jobTitle":"Vice President-Global Development","organisation":"Shelter Equity","email":"jgalland@shelterequity.org"},{"firstName":"Collince","lastName":"Goga","jobTitle":"Plant Operator","organisation":"Grain Industry Limited","email":"collincegoga@yahoo.com"}],"Email1":"info@asanteaid.org","Email2":"info@asanteaid.org","Address_country":"Kenya","Address_city":"KILIFI"}

Through formal registration, compliance, and coordination with district and provincial education authorities, GRACE complements public sector efforts to expand access, equity, and quality in education.
GRACE actively contributes to national and provincial goals on girls’ education by increasing enrollment, retention, and learning outcomes for girls in underserved mountain communities. Its inclusive education model supports children with disabilities through accessible schooling, teacher training, and community sensitization, directly advancing government commitments to inclusive and equitable education.
GRACE regularly engages government departments through approvals, reporting, participation in coordination meetings, and collaboration on teacher development, assessments, and school improvement initiatives. By piloting innovative, low cost models in inclusive and community based education, GRACE provides practical evidence that informs public education planning and strengthens state capacity to reach marginalized learners.","SingleLine2":"GRACE Association","MultiLine7":"GRACE Public School & College Skardu is a dynamic learning community and grassroots community rooted institution at the intersection of quality education, inclusion, and social responsibility and community development. Founded in a remote mountain context, GRACE serves girls, children with disabilities, and first-generation learners through inclusive schooling, teacher development, E STEAM learning, and strong community partnerships. The school actively integrates environmental awareness, digital skills, and leadership into everyday learning. GRACE also functions as a learning hub, sharing practice, mentoring educators, and collaborating with national and global partners to strengthen equitable education systems in underserved region of Skardu Gilgit-Baltistan, northern Pakistan.","SingleLine3":"+92 345 262 9124","MultiLine1":"GRACE envisages the socioeconomic aspirations of marginalised and economically vulnerable communities to create a prosperous and peaceful society.","SingleLine5":"CEO","MultiLine2":"GRACE has adopted two core values – social justice and equity and democracy – for its institutional norms and programmatic operations.","MultiLine3":"GRACE Association Pakistan works with the most marginalized and underprivileged communities in remote, mountainous regions of Gilgit-Baltistan and other parts of Pakistan. Rooted in strong organizational values, vision, and strategic principles, GRACE designs and implements evidence-based programs guided by a robust Monitoring and Evaluation Framework to ensure effectiveness, accountability, and measurable impact. Interim evaluations regularly assess relevance, sustainability, and outcomes, while learning informs continuous improvement.
Beyond long-term development, GRACE actively supports humanitarian response efforts during disasters and emergencies, working in coordination with local communities and partners.
Aligned with the national vision of uplifting the most vulnerable populations, GRACE has defined three core program areas for the next five to ten years. Quality Education focuses on inclusive schooling, teacher development, and E-STEAM learning for all children including girls and children with disabilities. Skills Enhancement and Employment promotes digital literacy, entrepreneurship, and workforce readiness for youth and women. Environment and Climate Change advances environmental education, climate resilience, and community-led conservation initiatives.","Address_zipCode":"44000","MultiLine4":"GRACE Association has made a sustained and measurable impact on expanding access to quality education for marginalized children, with a strong focus on girls and children with disabilities in Baltistan region of Gilgit Baltistan, northern Pakistan. Rooted in grassroots leadership, GRACE has established inclusive schools, after-school programs, and scholarship pathways that combine academic learning with life skills, digital literacy, and STEM education.
GRACE’s model challenges exclusion by enrolling children who were previously out of school due to poverty, disability, or gender norms, and by adapting teaching practices to diverse learning needs. Through teacher training, inclusive pedagogy, and community engagement, classrooms have become safer and more responsive spaces for all learners. Girls’ enrollment, retention, and confidence have improved significantly, while children with disabilities have gained visibility, dignity, and equal learning opportunities.
By linking local action with national and global partnerships, GRACE has strengthened education systems, influenced inclusive practices, and demonstrated that quality education for all is achievable, even in remote and resource-constrained contexts.","Number10":"55","Name_Last":"Hussain","MultipleChoice":["Pakistan"],"SingleLine31":"","SingleLine32":"","Dropdown":"Yes","SubForm1":[{"firstName":"Khadim","lastName":"Hussain","email7":"ceo@grace.org.pk"},{"firstName":"Mustafa","lastName":"Aqeel","email7":"principal@gracepublicschools.com"}],"MultipleChoice1":["ECED (3-6 years)","Grade 1","Grade 2","Grade 3","Grade 4","Grade 5","Grade 6","Grade 7","Grade 8","Grade 9","Grade 10"],"MultipleChoice4":null,"MultipleChoice3":["Childcare and ECED","Climate and education","Foundational literacy and numeracy","Girls education","Inclusive education","Secondary education and work readiness","Social and emotional learning"],"Dropdown9":"Yes","Name5_First":"Khadim","Name5_Last":"Hussain","Dropdown4":"Yes, all of the countries","Dropdown3":"Pakistan","Dropdown2":"Non-profit","Dropdown1":"Yes","Dropdown8":"Low income ($2.01 - $10 a day)","Dropdown6":"Affordable","SingleLine":"CEO","Dropdown5":"Less than $120","Dropdown10":"Yes","Dropdown11":"Yes","Dropdown13":"Yes, all our schools","Radio2":"Yes","Radio1":"Yes","Dropdown15":"GSF Website","MonthYear":"Feb-2007","Website":"www.grace.org.pk","Name_First":"Khadim","MultiLine":"","Name4_First":"Khadim","Name4_Last":"Hussain","Number":"5","Email6":"principal@gracepublicschools.com","SubForm":[{"firstName":"Khadim","lastName":"Hussain","jobTitle":"CEO","organisation":"GRACE Association","email":"ceo@grace.org.pk"},{"firstName":"Mustafa","lastName":"Aqeel","jobTitle":"Principal","organisation":"GRACE Public School & College Skardu","email":"principal@gracepublicschools.com"}],"Email1":"ceo@grace.org.pk","Email2":"ceo@grace.org.pk","Address_country":"Pakistan","Address_city":"Islamabad"}

Education & Digital Inclusion Program
We support access to quality education through school partnerships, community learning hubs, digital literacy training, and teacher support. Our work includes computer literacy, digital citizenship, life skills, and support for learners in low-resource schools to improve learning outcomes and future employability.

Maternal, Newborn & Community Health Program
We promote safe motherhood and community health by supporting pregnant women with clean birth education, maternal health awareness, referrals to health facilities, and partnerships with health workers. The program focuses on reducing preventable maternal and newborn risks through education and access to essential resources.

Women & Youth Empowerment Program
We work with women and youth groups to build skills for economic independence, leadership, and social participation. Activities include vocational skills, entrepreneurship training, and community savings and empowerment initiatives.

Community Infrastructure & Renewable Energy Support
We support the establishment of community hubs and essential infrastructure, including solar and digital solutions, to enable education, health outreach, and community services in off-grid and underserved areas.

Across all programs, we prioritize equity, sustainability, community participation, and partnerships to create lasting impact.","MultipleChoice1":["ECED (0-3 years)","ECED (3-6 years)","Grade 1","Grade 2","Grade 3","Grade 4","Grade 5","Grade 6","Grade 7","Grade 8","Grade 9","Grade 10","Grade 11","Grade 12"],"MultipleChoice3":["AI and education","Childcare and ECED","Climate and education","Education in emergencies","Foundational literacy and numeracy"],"Dropdown5":"More than $1000","Dropdown6":"Minimal contribution","Number":"5","Number1":"2000","Number2":"5000","Number10":"55","Number3":"300","Dropdown8":"Poor (less than $2 a day)","MultiLine4":"Ehaline Empowerment Initiative Center Uganda has created significant positive impact in education, health, and community development. Communities benefit from improved maternal health awareness, access to essential resources, and strengthened local infrastructure. Overall, our work enhances learning outcomes, gender equity, economic opportunity, and community resilience.","SingleLine31":"","SingleLine32":"","Dropdown9":"Yes","MultiLine5":"Ehaline Empowerment Initiative Center Uganda is a registered organization with the Uganda Registration Services Bureau (URSB) and actively registered with an operating License and Registration Certificates and collaborates with Jinja District Local Government to ensure alignment, coordination, and sustainability of our programs. We also engage with the Ministry of Education, local education offices, and health departments to support partner schools, implement digital literacy initiatives, and promote maternal and child health programs.

Our engagement includes:

Joint planning and coordination of community education and health initiatives.

Sharing program data and reports to inform local decision-making.

Leveraging government resources and networks to reach underserved populations.

Participating in policy dialogues and capacity-building workshops to strengthen program delivery.

These partnerships, combined with our formal registration with URSB and support from Jinja District Local Government, enhance the effectiveness, credibility, and sustainability of our interventions while fostering long-term community impact.","Dropdown10":"Yes","SingleLine3":"Mrs. Babirye Viola","Email6":"violab485@gmail.com","MultiLine7":"Ehaline Empowerment Initiative Center Uganda is a community-focused organization committed to empowering vulnerable populations through education, digital literacy, health awareness, and economic empowerment programs. Over the years, we have reached thousands of learners and community members, including women, youth, and children, providing critical skills, mentorship, and access to resources that improve learning outcomes, health practices, and economic opportunities. We actively collaborate with government agencies, schools, and local partners to maximize impact, sustainability, and inclusivity.

Our goal is to expand our programs and reach more underserved communities, and we welcome partnerships and support from organizations aligned with our mission to create lasting social impact.","Dropdown15":"GSF Website","SubForm":[{"firstName":"Rev.Canon Dr. Joy Mukisa","lastName":"Isabirye","jobTitle":"Dean Busoga Diocese, Senior Lecturer and Administrator Kyambogo University.","organisation":"Busoga Diocese and Kyambogo University","email":"joyisabirye@yahoo.com"},{"firstName":"Beth","lastName":"Beikirize","jobTitle":"Social Worker and Deputy Human Resource Officer","organisation":"Kampala International University Western Campus.","email":"betheliz2006@gmail.com"}],"Radio1":"Yes","Radio2":"Yes","SubForm1":[{"firstName":"ERIC","lastName":"MWEBAZA","email7":"ericmwebaza1@gmail.com"},{"firstName":"VIOLA","lastName":"BABIRYE","email7":"violab485@gmail.com"}]}

Our framework for social-emotional development is based on an international framework called CASEL. {"Address_address2":"Vinamra Khand, Gomti Nagar","Email":"viklangss@gmail.com","Address_address1":"3/193","Website1":"","Website2":"","Number3":"7","Formula":"60","Number2":"265","Number1":"65","MultiLine5":"","SingleLine2":"Agrani viklang Foundation","MultiLine7":"Our organization has been recognized for his lifelong contribution to disability inclusion and research. Our Founder Member, Shailendra Kumar Mishra, received the State Award from the Government of Uttar Pradesh on World Disability Day (December 3, 2009) and a Research Excellence Award (2022) for his dedicated work toward the upliftment of persons with disabilities. He has presented multiple research papers at prestigious international conferences in Mexico, Germany, Sri Lanka, and Europe (online) between 2018 and 2023, focusing on attitude change, empathy, self-efficacy, and pro-social behavior toward persons with disabilities. {"Address_address2":"41, Centro de Empresas PTS","Email":"mhernandez@ms2sgroup.com","Address_address1":"Avenida del Conocimiento","Website1":"https://www.linkedin.com/company/atenxia/","Website2":"https://x.com/atenxia_","Number3":"1200","Formula":"52","Number2":"20000","Number1":"10000","MultiLine5":"ATENXIA actively collaborates with public education and health systems to support early identification and intervention for attentional and learning difficulties.

We have worked with public institutions and government-affiliated organizations in Spain and Latin America, including pilot programs with public education bodies, school guidance and psychological services, and institutions linked to Ministries of Education. These collaborations focus on validating our evidence-based approach in real-world school settings, supporting inclusive education policies, and generating data to inform decision-making at a system level.

Through pilots, research collaborations, and ongoing dialogue with public authorities, ATENXIA contributes practical, scalable solutions that help governments address learning diversity, reduce school failure, and improve educational equity—particularly in contexts with limited access to specialist resources.","SingleLine2":"ATENXIA","MultiLine7":"ATENXIA combines scientific rigor, practical school implementation, and a strong commitment to educational equity.

Developed in close collaboration with leading academic research institutions, our methodology is grounded in evidence and continuously validated in real educational settings. At the same time, ATENXIA is designed to be practical and accessible for schools, requiring minimal training and resources to implement effectively.

We are particularly committed to working with schools and education systems serving vulnerable and underserved populations, where early support for learning and attention difficulties can have the greatest long-term impact. By joining the Global Schools Forum community, we hope to learn from peers, share evidence-based practices, and contribute to global efforts to strengthen inclusive, child-centered education systems.","SingleLine3":"Emilio Jimenez","MultiLine1":"ATENXIA’s vision is to ensure that every child can learn, focus, and thrive at school, regardless of attention difficulties, learning differences, or context.

We envision an education system where challenges such as ADHD and learning difficulties are identified early and addressed through personalized, evidence-based interventions integrated into everyday school life. By combining artificial intelligence with scientifically validated methodologies developed in collaboration with leading research institutions, ATENXIA empowers schools to deliver individualized support at scale.

Our long-term vision is to help schools become more inclusive, effective, and equitable, reducing school failure and its social consequences while improving academic performance, wellbeing, and long-term outcomes for students. We aim to work alongside schools, educators, and education systems worldwide—especially in underserved communities—to transform how learning difficulties are supported, ensuring that no child is left behind due to lack of personalized attention.","SingleLine5":"CoFounder","MultiLine2":"ATENXIA’s mission is to support schools in improving students’ attention, executive functions, and learning skills through personalized, evidence-based digital interventions.

We work with schools, educators, and specialists to identify and address attentional and learning difficulties early, using artificial intelligence to adapt scientifically validated exercises to each child’s needs. Our mission is to make high-quality, research-backed support accessible, scalable, and easy to integrate into daily school practice, helping educators respond effectively to neurodiversity.

By bridging science and education, ATENXIA aims to reduce learning gaps, prevent school failure, and improve academic outcomes and wellbeing for children—particularly those who are most at risk of being left behind.","MultiLine3":"ATENXIA’s core program is a school-based digital intervention designed to improve attention, executive functions, and learning-related skills in children with ADHD, learning difficulties, and related challenges.

The program uses artificial intelligence to deliver personalized cognitive training exercises that adapt in real time to each student’s performance, ensuring an individualized learning path. Interventions are grounded in scientifically validated methodologies developed in collaboration with the University of Granada’s research centers and are designed to be implemented within the school day.

Schools begin with an initial assessment and configuration process, after which students engage in short, structured training sessions over several weeks. Educators and specialists have access to dashboards that monitor progress, generate actionable insights, and support data-informed decision-making. The program can be used both for targeted intervention and preventive support, helping schools identify difficulties early and respond before academic failure occurs.

ATENXIA’s model is scalable, easy to deploy, and adaptable to different educational contexts, making it suitable for diverse school systems, including those with limited specialist resources.","Address_zipCode":"18016","MultiLine4":"ATENXIA helps schools improve students’ attention, learning skills, and academic outcomes while reducing the risk of school failure and exclusion.

By enabling early identification and personalized intervention for attentional and learning difficulties, ATENXIA empowers educators to support neurodiverse students more effectively within the classroom. We have worked with public institutions and government-affiliated organizations in Spain and Latin America, including pilot programs with public education bodies, school guidance and psychological services, and institutions linked to Ministries of Education. These collaborations focus on validating our evidence-based approach in real-world school settings, supporting inclusive education policies, and generating data to inform decision-making at a system level.

Through pilots, research collaborations, and ongoing dialogue with public authorities, ATENXIA contributes practical, scalable solutions that help governments address learning diversity, reduce school failure, and improve educational equity—particularly in contexts with limited access to specialist resources.","SingleLine2":"ATENXIA","MultiLine7":"ATENXIA combines scientific rigor, practical school implementation, and a strong commitment to educational equity.

Developed in close collaboration with leading academic research institutions, our methodology is grounded in evidence and continuously validated in real educational settings. At the same time, ATENXIA is designed to be practical and accessible for schools, requiring minimal training and resources to implement effectively.

We are particularly committed to working with schools and education systems serving vulnerable and underserved populations, where early support for learning and attention difficulties can have the greatest long-term impact. By joining the Global Schools Forum community, we hope to learn from peers, share evidence-based practices, and contribute to global efforts to strengthen inclusive, child-centered education systems.","SingleLine3":"Emilio Jimenez","MultiLine1":"ATENXIA’s vision is to ensure that every child can learn, focus, and thrive at school, regardless of attention difficulties, learning differences, or context.

We envision an education system where challenges such as ADHD and learning difficulties are identified early and addressed through personalized, evidence-based interventions integrated into everyday school life. By combining artificial intelligence with scientifically validated methodologies developed in collaboration with leading research institutions, ATENXIA empowers schools to deliver individualized support at scale.

Our long-term vision is to help schools become more inclusive, effective, and equitable, reducing school failure and its social consequences while improving academic performance, wellbeing, and long-term outcomes for students. We aim to work alongside schools, educators, and education systems worldwide—especially in underserved communities—to transform how learning difficulties are supported, ensuring that no child is left behind due to lack of personalized attention.","SingleLine5":"CoFounder","MultiLine2":"ATENXIA’s mission is to support schools in improving students’ attention, executive functions, and learning skills through personalized, evidence-based digital interventions.

We work with schools, educators, and specialists to identify and address attentional and learning difficulties early, using artificial intelligence to adapt scientifically validated exercises to each child’s needs. Our mission is to make high-quality, research-backed support accessible, scalable, and easy to integrate into daily school practice, helping educators respond effectively to neurodiversity.

By bridging science and education, ATENXIA aims to reduce learning gaps, prevent school failure, and improve academic outcomes and wellbeing for children—particularly those who are most at risk of being left behind.","MultiLine3":"ATENXIA’s core program is a school-based digital intervention designed to improve attention, executive functions, and learning-related skills in children with ADHD, learning difficulties, and related challenges.

The program uses artificial intelligence to deliver personalized cognitive training exercises that adapt in real time to each student’s performance, ensuring an individualized learning path. Interventions are grounded in scientifically validated methodologies developed in collaboration with the University of Granada’s research centers and are designed to be implemented within the school day.

Schools begin with an initial assessment and configuration process, after which students engage in short, structured training sessions over several weeks. Educators and specialists have access to dashboards that monitor progress, generate actionable insights, and support data-informed decision-making. The program can be used both for targeted intervention and preventive support, helping schools identify difficulties early and respond before academic failure occurs.

ATENXIA’s model is scalable, easy to deploy, and adaptable to different educational contexts, making it suitable for diverse school systems, including those with limited specialist resources.","Address_zipCode":"18016","MultiLine4":"ATENXIA helps schools improve students’ attention, learning skills, and academic outcomes while reducing the risk of school failure and exclusion.

{"Address_address2":"off Komarock road","Email":"amuhonja@gmail.com","Address_address1":"Kangundo road","Website1":"linkedin.com/in/alice-m-44426078/","Website2":"","Number3":"35","Number2":"7000","Number1":"1000","MultiLine5":"Safisha Africa Welfare Foundation works in close partnership with government institutions and community leadership structures to ensure that support reaches the most vulnerable children and is delivered transparently and sustainably.
Identification and Referral of Vulnerable Children:
Government officers, including Children’s Officers, Chiefs, Assistant Chiefs, and Nyumba Kumi (Ten-House) community leaders, support Safisha by identifying children who are out of school, at risk of dropping out, or living in extreme vulnerability. These children are formally referred to Safisha Africa School for admission and support
Vetting and Accountability:
Admissions are conducted through a community-based vetting process involving Nyumba Kumi leaders and local administration to confirm a family’s vulnerability. This ensures that Safisha’s services reach children who genuinely need support and strengthens transparency and accountability in program delivery
Registration and Oversight by the Ministry of Education:
Safisha Africa School is fully registered under the Ministry of Education and operates in compliance with national education policies and standards. The school follows the approved curriculum and is regularly monitored through education officers.
National Examinations and Transition to Public Secondary Schools:
Learners at Safisha sit for national examinations as required. Those who perform well are selected and enrolled into government secondary schools, ensuring continuity of education and full integration into the national education system.
Shared Commitment to Child Welfare and Retention:
Through this collaboration, Safisha and government partners jointly address school dropout, child protection, and access to education, ensuring children not only enroll in school but remain, perform well, and progress through the education system.
This partnership with government structures strengthens Safisha’s impact, aligns the organization with national development priorities, and ensures long-term sustainability of its programs.","SingleLine2":"Safisha Africa Welfare Foundation","MultiLine7":"we will be happy to be part of this community  to expand our network and learn from others","SingleLine3":"Stephen Masibo","MultiLine1":"To empower and develop every child from under-resourced families through access to education, so they can thrive.","SingleLine5":"Executive Director","MultiLine2":"Safisha Africa Welfare Foundation is dedicated to transforming the lives of vulnerable children and women in underserved communities by providing free access to education, nutrition, healthcare, and economic empowerment. We build and run schools through our JENGA program, support learners through sponsorships, feeding, and medical care, and empower women with opportunities for economic independence and leadership. Our mission is to break cycles of poverty, promote peace and equality, and create sustainable opportunities that enable every child and woman to thrive and realize their full potential.","MultiLine3":"Safisha Africa Welfare Foundation – Core Programs
1. Education
   Access to quality schooling for children from under-resourced families
    Construction of schools and learning facilities
2. School Feeding & Nutrition
    Daily meals for children, often their only reliable nutrition
    Promotes attendance, concentration, and learning outcomes
3. Medical Care & Health Support
    Basic medical services, referrals, and life-saving interventions
4. Girls’ & Women Empowerment
     Livelihood support, skills development, and small business initiatives
     Focus on adolescent mothers and vulnerable women
5. Environmental Sustainability & Agriculture
   Climate-resilient kitchen farming
   Fruit tree planting programs
    Environmental education to foster community responsibility","Address_zipCode":"00200","MultiLine4":"Impact of Safisha Africa Welfare Foundation
Since its founding in 2007, Safisha Africa Welfare Foundation has delivered life-changing, sustainable, and long-term impact** for children and women from under-resourced communities in Kenya.
Transforming Access to Education
Enabled over 7,000 children from poverty-stricken backgrounds to access and remain in school
Constructed schools in underserved areas to bring quality education to communities that previously had no access
Improving Child Health and Nutrition
 Provided school feeding programs reaching over 10,000 children, often the only reliable daily meal
 Ensured medical care for over 3,000 children, including life-saving interventions
Empowering Women and Adolescent Mothers
Supported over 1,000 women and adolescent mothers through livelihood programs, small business initiatives, and skills development
 Strengthened women’s economic stability to keep children in school and foster resilient communities
Promoting Environmental Sustainability
 Integrated climate-resilient kitchen farming and fruit tree planting in schools and communities
 Promoted environmental awareness to improve child nutrition, food security, and sustainable community practices
Long-Term Community Transformation
Safisha’s integrated approach—combining education, nutrition, healthcare, women’s empowerment, and sustainable agriculture—has created healthier, educated, and more resilient communities, breaking cycles of poverty and empowering children to thrive.","Number10":"40","Name_Last":"Muhonja","MultipleChoice":["Kenya"],"SingleLine31":"","SingleLine32":"","Dropdown":"Yes","SubForm1":[{"firstName":"Alice","lastName":"Muhonja","email7":"amuhonja@gmail.com"},{"firstName":"Grace","lastName":"Odhiambo","email7":"gnabuala@gmail.com"}],"MultipleChoice1":["ECED (0-3 years)","ECED (3-6 years)","Grade 1","Grade 2","Grade 3"],"MultipleChoice4":null,"MultipleChoice3":["Childcare and ECED","Foundational literacy and numeracy"],"Dropdown9":"Yes","Name5_First":"Alice","Name5_Last":"Muhonja","Dropdown4":"Yes, all of the countries","Dropdown3":"Kenya","Dropdown2":"Non-profit","Dropdown1":"Yes","Dropdown8":"Poor (less than $2 a day)","Dropdown6":"Free","SingleLine":"Executive Director","Dropdown5":"Zero fees","Dropdown10":"Yes","Dropdown11":"No","Dropdown13":"Yes, all our schools","Radio2":"Yes","Radio1":"Yes","Dropdown15":"GSF Website","MonthYear":"Mar-2010","Website":"www.safishaafrica.org","Name_First":"Alice","MultiLine":"","Name4_First":"Alice","Name4_Last":"Muhonja","Number":"10","Email6":"simiyustevens@gmail.com","SubForm":[{"firstName":"Regina","lastName":"Karanja","jobTitle":"Partner","organisation":"Rockefeller Foundation","email":"RKaranja@rockfound.org"},{"firstName":"Nanda Daisy","lastName":"Nabwire","jobTitle":"Beneficiary","organisation":"Safisha Africa Welfare Foundation","email":"nabwiredaisy42@gmail.com"}],"Email1":"amuhonja@gmail.com","Email2":"amuhonja@gmail.com","Address_country":"Kenya","Address_city":"Nairobi"}

{"Address_address2":"","Email":"devyani@prathaminternational.org","Address_address1":"8 The Green, Suite B","Website1":"https://www.linkedin.com/company/prathaminternational/","Website2":"https://x.com/Pratham_Intl","Number3":"1","Formula":"50","Number2":"1063000","Number1":"1014000","MultiLine5":"Pratham International partners with government education systems to provide technical support, training, and mentoring so interventions like Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) can be embedded within regular school programs. In response to the earlier question about our fees, we have not specified an amount because the cost of technical assistance depends on the scope of work and the nature of our engagement, which varies by context.

Similarly, we do not typically track the number of teachers directly impacted through our programs, hence, we have not put in any value for the same.

Finally, we work in a range of countries including low and middle income countries.","SingleLine3":"Pragya Dhariwal","MultiLine1":"Every child and young person reaching their full potential","SingleLine5":"Chief Programs Officer","MultiLine2":"Our purpose is to start with the problem and work from the ground up – partnering with stakeholders and systems to build joyful, measurable learning solutions to grow potential for children and youth.","MultiLine3":"At the core of our work is the support and adaptation of the Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) approach, pioneered by Pratham in India. This is an evidence-based intervention designed to help children in Grade 3 and above catch up on foundational skills in reading and mathematics. The model works by grouping children based on their actual learning levels rather than their age or grade, enabling rapid progress over a short period.
This flexible approach can be adapted by NGOs, governments, and communities in various ways to suit local contexts.
To reduce the number of children reaching higher grades with foundational learning gaps, we have recently begun supporting adaptations of Pratham’s Leap Forward intervention. This targets children entering Grade 1 and those in Grades 1 and 2 through a combination of school- and community-based instructional and awareness building methods. The aim is to build critical foundational literacy and numeracy (FLN) skills early on, so that fewer children advance through the education system without these essential competencies.","Address_zipCode":"DE 19901","MultiLine4":"We define the impact of our work as improvements in foundational reading and math skills among children, achieved through government- and local partner‑led TaRL programs.  Using simple, one‑on‑one tools inspired by ASER, children’s reading and maths skills are evaluated at baseline (at the start), midline (in the middle), and endline (at the end) of the intervention. Progress is often tracked by the percentage of children who can read at least a simple paragraph (Grade 1 level) and solve a basic subtraction problem by the end of the intervention. 

For exampls, in Brazil, as per partner reported data, there was a 34 percentage point (pp)improvement in the proportion of children who could read at least a simple paragraph in Portuguese by the end of the intervention. This support has strengthened our ability to tackle challenges such as child labour and learner absenteeism in our community. Through family engagement, awareness campaigns, and consistent learner follow-ups, we encourage regular school attendance and help protect children’s right to education. The grant has enabled us to create safer, more supportive learning environments where children can remain in school and benefit fully from our foundational learning programme.","SingleLine3":"Samuel Yeboah","MultiLine1":"A future where every child can read, write, and lead with confidence.","SingleLine5":"Executive Director","MultiLine2":"To ignite foundational literacy and numeracy skills among Ghanaian Primary school learners","MultiLine3":"We are a community-driven initiative focused on improving foundational literacy and numeracy skills in underserved areas. Through the Teaching at the Right Level programs, we empower learners and educators to achieve sustainable growth.","Address_zipCode":"ESS18","MultiLine4":"Our work strengthens foundational learning for children in underserved communities by using the evidence-based Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) approach.
