1. School Feeding Programme
This programme provides nutritious meals to children in vulnerable public schools in order to improve their health, increase school attendance and enhance their ability to concentrate and perform well in class. 2. Education Sponsorship Programme (Primary and Secondary)
This programme supports vulnerable but deserving learners by covering school fees and the associated school levies. Additionally, we provide essential learning materials such as uniforms and stationery. We also offer comprehensive mentorship to the beneficiaries to cater for their mental health and ensure they remain motivated to learn. It prevents school dropout and enables children from disadvantaged backgrounds to complete their basic education.

3. WOVEN – Women of Vision Education Programme (Tertiary Level)
WOVEN empowers young women by providing education scholarships, mentorship and leadership development opportunities for university and vocational education. The programme focuses on reducing gender inequality in access to higher education and nurturing future female leaders. We also endeavour to withdraw barriers to learning especially those attributed to poverty. 

4. Wezesha Programme (Empowerment and Sustainability)
This is our sustainability strategy to ensure that schools and households are able to feed their children to sustain our school feeding interventiosn. Adolescent Development Program: Enabling schools to provide holistic education to their students","Dropdown12":"Students","MultipleChoice1":["Grade 5","Grade 6","Grade 7","Grade 8","Grade 9","Grade 10"],"MultipleChoice2":["Curriculum design and development","Education technology","Remediation support","School development and improvement"],"MultipleChoice3":["AI and education","Foundational literacy and numeracy"],"Dropdown5":"No","Dropdown6":"","Number11":"","Number":"60","Number1":"10000","Number2":"11000","Number10":"50","Formula":"50","Number3":"1000","Dropdown8":"Poor (less than $2 a day)","MultiLine4":"Our ADP network extends to over 60 schools, community centres, and orphanages, from 5 states (Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, and Goa), resulting in a positive impact over 11,000 students.

363 college students from 8 states (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Rajasthan, UP, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Orissa, and Goa), have benefited under the HHE program till date. Out of these, 203 are alumni, who have already graduated, while the other 160 are still in college.

84% of our alumni are employed, 9% are pursuing higher studies, and 3% are preparing for competitive exams such as the UPSC.  Of the remaining, 1% are homemakers, 1% seeking employment, and 2% have unfortunately expired.

We recently launched a survey of our alumni who have been working for more than a year, to understand the wider impact of our HHE program. Based on the responses that have come in till date, following are a few key findings that very effectively underline the impact that higher education has made to the lives of our alumni, their families, and their communities:

•	Secondary Beneficiaries: Over 63% of our alumni support the education of 1 or more others. For those supporting more than 1, the average number of others being supported works out to 2.8. •	Better lives for their families: Over 36% support the monthly expenses of their family either fully or partially. 58% not only support the monthly expenses, but have gone beyond and also supported capital expenses such as construction/buying/improvement of home, buying appliances and equipment at home/farm/shop etc., resulting in a better quality of life for the entire family","SingleLine31":"","SingleLine32":"","Dropdown9":"No","MultiLine5":"","Dropdown10":"Yes","SingleLine3":"dr Vaijayanati Deogekar","Email6":"vdeogekar@gmail.com","MultiLine7":"We are largely volunteer driven organization with admin cost at around 2%PA.","Dropdown15":"GSF member","SubForm":[{"firstName":"sunil","lastName":"Dodeja","jobTitle":"Group Director","organisation":"General Manufacturing and Trading Corporation","email":"sdodeja63@gmail.com"},{"firstName":"Vijay","lastName":"Khare","jobTitle":"Director","organisation":"Softtek","email":"Vijay.P.Khare@gmail.com"}],"Radio1":"Yes","Radio2":"Yes","SubForm1":[{"firstName":"Pradeep","lastName":"Waychal","email7":"pradeep.waychal@gurujifoudation.in"},{"firstName":"Priyanka","lastName":"Nikte","email7":"accounts@gurujifoundation.in"}]}

While the current focus is on consolidating operations within these areas, there is an intention to expand gradually once funding, staffing, and systems are strengthened.","MultiLine1":"We envision a Nigeria where every child thrives in a safe, nurturing, and developmentally rich early childhood environment supported by empowered parents, well-trained childcare providers, and community-driven systems that uphold the highest standards of care and learning.","MultiLine2":"To ensure every Nigerian child in the early years has access to affordable, high-quality, nurturing childcare by strengthening childcare systems, empowering parents, engaging communities, and advocating for supportive national policies.","MultiLine3":"Community Childcare Project (CCP): The CCP is our flagship model for upgrading childcare quality in informal and formal settings. The organisation tracks attendance for both online and in-person sessions, administers module-based tests aligned to each pillar of the curriculum, and collects qualitative feedback from parents. Practical monitoring tools include spot checks, unannounced visits, follow-up calls to parents, and verification of whether provided resources—such as hygiene kits, first-aid kits, and communication booklets—are being used appropriately. The organisation has begun experimenting with digital data collection tools such as KoboCollect but is still developing its systems. Programme retention currently stands at approximately 70%. ","SingleLine32":"No external evaluation has yet been conducted, and strengthening M&E systems has been identified as a priority.","Dropdown9":"No","MultiLine5":"","Dropdown10":"Yes","SingleLine3":"Bassey Umoh","Email6":"hello@neccsi.org","MultiLine7":"","Dropdown15":"GSF member","SubForm":[{"firstName":"Patrick","lastName":"Higdon","jobTitle":"Global Director of Programs","organisation":"World Connect","email":"patrick@worldconnect-global.org"},{"firstName":"Oluwafunmilayo","lastName":"Gombe","jobTitle":"Founder","organisation":"The Event Nanny Community Childcare Initiative","email":"oagombe@theeventnanny.com.ng"}],"Radio1":"Yes","Radio2":"Yes","SubForm1":[{"firstName":"Pamela","lastName":"Akinboboye","email7":"pamela@icarella.com"},{"firstName":"Margaret","lastName":"Akinware","email7":"margaret.akinware@gmail.com"}],"SingleLine11":"The Nurturing Early Childhood Community Support Initiative (NECCSI), also referred to as the “Next Initiative,” was formally registered as a non-governmental organisation on 1 November 2025, although its work began earlier in 2024 as a project. The organisation emerged from the Community Childcare Project, which was funded by World Connect. This initial project focused on supporting home-based, centre-based, and community-based childcare providers through capacity building, advocacy, and the creation of peer support networks. The decision to formally register the organisation was driven by the need to attract further funding, institutionalise the work, and expand its impact. The core motivation behind the initiative is to address the significant policy and service gap affecting childcare for children aged 0–3 years in Nigeria, a group that is largely unsupported by existing education and social systems.","SingleLine12":"The organisation has so far received a single seed grant of approximately USD 4,000–4,400 from World Connect, which supported activities between 2024 and 2025. Although eligible for additional funding cycles under the same programme, the organisation did not apply immediately due to the need to first complete registration and demonstrate proof of concept. An additional USD 1,000 was contributed through the founder’s participation in the World Forum Global Leaders for Early Childhood Fellowship. At present, funding remains limited and largely grant-dependent.","SingleLine17":"The organisation’s programme model centres on training childcare providers who serve children aged 0–3 years, with some flexibility to include children up to age five depending on context. To date, three cohorts of childcare providers have successfully completed the programme, and preparations are underway for a fourth cohort. The training runs for ten weeks and is delivered through a blended model combining online learning and in-person sessions. The curriculum covers early childhood development, the five pillars of the Nurturing Care Framework, and practical guidance on childcare business formalisation and registration. Beyond direct training, the programme incorporates community-level impact through step-down training, where caregivers train peers, and parent awareness sessions focused on nutrition and responsive caregiving, sometimes reaching up to 100 parents per session. The long-term vision is to build credible evidence that can be used to advocate for policy reform and improved regulation of early childcare services. To improve sustainability, the organisation has introduced modest income-generating strategies, including charging a token registration and training fee, selling training materials such as caregiver–parent communication booklets, and supporting caregivers to generate income through the resale of nutrition products to parents. Despite these efforts, funding constraints remain a key limitation to scale and staffing.","SingleLine13":"The governance structure is currently lean and founder-led. The organisation is overseen by a three-member executive board comprising the founder and two senior women who serve in both governance and operational roles.Governance systems and policies are still evolving as the organisation transitions from an early-stage setup toward a more formal structure. ","SingleLine14":"The governance structure is currently lean and founder-led. The organisation is overseen by a three-member executive board comprising the founder and two senior women who serve in both governance and operational roles.","SingleLine28":"With regard to curriculum and regulation, the organisation does not rely on a nationally enforced early childhood curriculum for children aged 0–3, as existing government guidance is outdated and not actively implemented. Instead, the organisation has developed and continuously refined its own curriculum based on the globally recognised Nurturing Care Framework. While the childcare sector remains largely unregulated, NECCSI is registered with and accountable to the Ministry of Youth and Social Welfare, which oversees organisations working with vulnerable populations. However, the regulatory environment remains challenging, particularly for home-based childcare providers who are often penalised rather than supported.","SingleLine29":"From a costing perspective, the organisation estimates that it costs approximately USD 300 to fully train one childcare provider when training materials, facilitation, resources, and community engagement are factored in. This figure is based on internal calculations and remains indicative, as the organisation continues to refine its costing and financial models. The relatively high per-provider cost underscores the importance of securing sustainable funding streams.","MultiLine6":"Not Applicable","SingleLine8":"Not Applicable","SingleLine33":"Key strengths of the organisation include its deep integration within the communities it serves and its ability to deliver training in local languages and dialects. The programme is highly practical and experiential, making it accessible and relevant to caregivers with varying levels of formal education. Caregivers report strong engagement and increased confidence, and parents have responded positively to improved childcare practices. The founder’s background in childcare services, training, and child development further strengthens the organisation’s credibility and delivery model.","SingleLine34":"The organisation faces several challenges. Limited funding restricts the ability to hire staff, expand monitoring activities, and scale operations. The small team makes it difficult to conduct frequent field visits and provide ongoing hands-on support to caregivers. Additionally, while data is being collected, there is a recognised need for stronger research design, data analysis capacity, and structured learning systems to ensure the evidence generated can influence policy and attract larger funders.","SingleLine35":"The organisation sees membership in the Global Schools Forum as a critical opportunity to address these gaps. Its motivation for joining includes access to structured learning, technical support, peer exchange, and guidance on governance, monitoring and evaluation, costing, and sustainability. The organisation is also interested in potential incubator programmes and funding pathways that could enable responsible growth.","SingleLine36":"The organisation believes it can contribute meaningfully to the GSF community by sharing practitioner-level insights and data from Nigeria’s early childcare landscape, a context that is underrepresented in global evidence. The founder also brings strong teaching and mentoring skills and is keen to support peer learning within the community while contributing grounded, grassroots perspectives on early childhood care.","Number4":"11"}

{"Name_First":"Tom","Name_Last":"Ravenscroft","SingleLine":"CEO","SingleLine2":"Skills Builder Partnership","Email":"tom@skillsbuilder.org","Website":"www.skillsbuilder.org","Website1":"https://www.linkedin.com/company/skills-builder-global/","Website2":"","Dropdown":"Yes","Name5_First":"Tom","Name5_Last":"Ravenscroft","Email1":"tom@skillsbuilder.org","Dropdown1":"Yes","Name4_First":"Tom","Name4_Last":"Ravenscroft","SingleLine5":"CEO","Email2":"tom@skillsbuilder.org","MonthYear":"Jun-2009","Dropdown2":"Non-profit","Dropdown3":"United Kingdom","MultipleChoice":["Czechia","Hong Kong SAR, China","India","Kenya","Lebanon","Nigeria","Uganda","United Kingdom"],"Dropdown4":"No, none of the countries outside HQ","MultiLine":"Our model is focused on working with local partners and supporting them to adapt and use the Skills Builder model to work in their context.","SingleLine11":"Founded by Tom Ravenscroft, who started the organisation after working as a teacher in the UK and identifying a gap in education systems around explicitly teaching broader, transferable skills (such as communication, collaboration and self-management). The organisation began as an effort to develop and scale a structured approach to building these skills for learners.","SingleLine12":"The organisation is a not-for-profit funded through a mixed model including:  Grants and support from foundations (particularly corporate foundations)  Fee-for-service work with corporates (used to cross-subsidise education work)  Financial contributions from some schools, colleges and NGO partners, varying by country and ability to pay","SingleLine13":"Governed by an independent non-executive board (approximately five members) and supported by a wider advisory group of around 30 members, including partners, funders, educators, policy experts, academics and sector leaders.","Number4":"41","MultiLine1":"Our vision is to ensure that one day, everyone has the essential skills to thrive. 

We define essential skills as those highly transferable skills that almost everyone needs to do almost any job and which support the application of technical skills and knowledge. They are listening, speaking, problem solving, creativity, teamwork, leadership, planning, and adapting.","MultiLine2":"Our mission is to transform how the world builds essential skills by uniting education, NGOs, employers, and government around the Skills Builder Universal Framework. We provide the common language, tools, and professional development to embed these skills systematically and across learning and working contexts with our partners.","MultiLine3":"Our core programmes globally are delivered through a proven four-stage model designed for maximum scale and systemic impact, all centred around the Skills Builder Universal Framework:

1. Schools & Colleges: We partner directly with schools and colleges (in over 20 countries) to run the Accelerator programme, investing in Skills Leaders and providing comprehensive teacher training and resources to drive rapid, measurable progress in essential skills.

2. Local NGO Partnerships: We collaborate with local Non-Governmental Organisations and training providers globally to embed the Framework into their existing programmes, offering upskilling and quantifying the impact on their beneficiaries.

3. National Lead Partners: We establish long-term partnerships with credible national champions to adapt, translate, and scale the approach across an entire country's ecosystem, building a local provider network.

4. System Strengthening: We engage with governments and education systems (e.g., in Kenya and Uganda) to build the Universal Framework into the national curriculum, teacher training, and school inspection regimes, ensuring sustainable, whole-system change for all learners.","Dropdown12":"Students","MultipleChoice1":["ECED (3-6 years)","Grade 1","Grade 2","Grade 3","Grade 4","Grade 5","Grade 6","Grade 7","Grade 8","Grade 9","Grade 10","Grade 11","Grade 12"],"MultipleChoice2":["Curriculum design and development","Education technology","Learning outcomes assessments","School development and improvement","School leader development and certification","System strengthening","Teacher development and certification","Teaching and learning material"],"MultipleChoice3":["Inclusive education","Secondary education and work readiness","Social and emotional learning"],"Dropdown5":"No","Dropdown6":"","Number11":"","SingleLine28":"The Skills Builder Universal Framework is aligned with national frameworks where they exist. In England, it is included in statutory guidance for schools. In other countries, it is either mapped to existing national skills frameworks or adopted where no equivalent framework exists.","SingleLine29":"Costs vary significantly by context and delivery partner. In the UK, average costs are approximately £1–£2 per child per year. Costs are lower in some other contexts due to cross-subsidisation and partner-led delivery.","Number":"907","MultiLine6":"Primarily government schools and low-cost private schools. In the UK, the organisation works exclusively with government schools. In other countries, delivery includes government and low-cost private school settings. ","Number1":"2462000","Number2":"6700000","Number10":"50","Formula":"50","Number3":"22729","Dropdown8":"Middle income ($10.01 - $20 a day)","MultiLine4":"Our approach is proven to significantly accelerate essential skills development. Learners on the Accelerator programme achieve 1.52 average steps of progress per skill per year, an acceleration of up to 3.0x compared to baseline. The Skills Builder Universal Framework has been tried and tested with over 5 million learners in the UK, is used in over 80% of English secondary schools, and is built into UK government statutory guidance, demonstrating robust, scalable impact.","SingleLine31":"Data is collected primarily through teacher-led assessments aligned to the Skills Builder Framework, conducted at the beginning and end of the programme cycle. Online tools are used where feasible, with paper-based approaches adapted for lower-resource contexts. Comparative analysis is used to assess value-add.","SingleLine32":"Evaluation is primarily conducted internally through the organisation’s data systems, with external reviews and assessments commissioned periodically. Impact findings are published annually in public impact reports.","Dropdown9":"Yes","MultiLine5":"We have worked at a governmental level in the UK, Uganda and Kenya. In these cases, we have worked as a technical expert to support the development of effective ways of assessing and tracking essential skills over time and setting age-related expectations.","Dropdown10":"Yes","SingleLine3":"Evelyn Haywood","Email6":"evelyn.haywood@skillsbuilder.org","MultiLine7":"Having joined the GSF Annual Meeting in Nairobi this year, I'm excited about Skills Builder joining such an impressive and aligned group of organisations. While our work spans a variety of countries and contexts, our primary focus is on developing countries where our partnerships with local NGOs and school groups have proved so fruitful.","SingleLine34":"Still early in the journey of adapting and embedding the model across diverse international contexts  Need for deeper local contextual expertise in new geographies  Developing consistent data collection approaches in lower-resource settings","Dropdown15":"GSF member","SubForm":[{"firstName":"Jenny","lastName":"Groot","jobTitle":"CEO","organisation":"PEAS","email":"jenny.groot@peas.org.uk"},{"firstName":"Susan","lastName":"Douglas","jobTitle":"Education Advisor","organisation":"British Council","email":"Susan.Douglas@britishcouncil.org"}],"Radio1":"Yes","Radio2":"Yes","SubForm1":[{"firstName":"Tom","lastName":"Ravenscroft","email7":"tom@skillsbuilder.org"},{"firstName":"Sophie","lastName":"Deaville","email7":"sophie.deaville@skillsbuilder.org"}],"SingleLine14":"Senior leaders and advisors are typically drawn from:  Leaders of major partner organisations  Individuals with deep expertise in specific geographies or education segments  Experts in education policy, academia, social enterprise, business leadership and campaigning The composition is intentionally diverse to reflect multiple perspectives.","SingleLine15":"Currently, all core team members are based in the UK. The organisation is exploring decentralising and locating team members in other geographies as international work expands.","SingleLine17":"The organisation is focused on:  Expanding international partnerships and testing the framework across multiple contexts (approximately 50 countries to date)  Identifying and supporting credible “lead partners” (local NGOs) to build country-level ecosystems  Deepening engagement in selected countries (e.g. Nigeria, Uganda, Kenya) rather than directly implementing everywhere Growth is supported through continued cross-subsidisation and diversified income streams.","SingleLine8":"The model prioritises embedding capacity within schools rather than long-term dependency. After an intensive one-year engagement, schools are expected to continue independently, with optional access to shared resources and peer learning rather than repeated programme renewal","SingleLine33":"Clear, structured and open-source skills framework applicable across ages and contexts  Strong emphasis on partnership and capacity-building rather than direct delivery  Diverse funding model enabling cross-subsidisation  Credibility with schools, NGOs and employers  Alignment with education systems and policy frameworks","SingleLine35":"GSF offers access to aligned organisations, learning opportunities across diverse contexts, peer exchange, and trusted networks to support international expansion, partnership development and shared learning.","SingleLine36":"The organisation can contribute open-source tools, learning from large-scale skills development, experience running structured communities of practice, and practical insights on embedding skills frameworks within education systems."}

The Sierra Leone Educators Association (SLEA) delivers a suite of integrated programs designed to holistically address the educational ecosystem. Our initiatives target students, teachers, schools, and communities to foster sustainable development and empower the next generation of leaders.

1. Literacy for All Program
We combat illiteracy through comprehensive, evidence-based initiatives that equip learners of all ages with foundational competencies in reading, writing, and critical comprehension. Our programs are implemented in both school and community settings to ensure nationwide impact.

2. Teacher Empowerment Initiative
Recognizing that teachers are the cornerstone of quality education, we provide continuous professional development. Our training modules focus on modern pedagogical techniques, subject-matter mastery, and psychosocial support, fostering a valued, motivated, and highly effective teaching force.

3. Human Rights & Civic Education
We are dedicated to weaving the principles of human rights and civic responsibility into the fabric of society. Through targeted engagement with students, youth, teachers, and parents, we build a culture of awareness, respect, and active citizenship.

4. Green Schools & Community Action Program
This program transforms schools into vibrant hubs for environmental stewardship. Using a hands-on, practical model, students lead projects in school gardening, reforestation, and community clean-ups, directly linking learning to sustainable development.

5. Youth Skills & Entrepreneurship Development
We bridge the gap between education and economic opportunity by providing youth and women with market-relevant skills training. Our curriculum encompasses technical and vocational skills, digital literacy, and essential soft skills to enhance employability and entrepreneurial success.

6. School Health & Well-being Advocacy
A healthy learner is a productive learner. We advocate for and educate on public health within schools and communities, promoting practices that ensure the physical and mental well-being necessary for effective learning and a high quality of life.

7. School Infrastructure & Learning Resources
We believe a conducive learning environment is fundamental.
